newsitem.title: CHINA: RTRS-China 1997 wool imports seen low.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-China 1997 wool imports seen low.

text.p: China's wool imports will increase slightly this year but were expected to remain well down from levels in 1995, the China Daily said on Monday.

The low level of imports was expected to continue for some time, partly because of a shortage of funds among many domestic wool-spinning enterprises and rising inventories of finished wool and worsted products because of poor textile sales, it said.

China's wool sector faces a structural crisis, it quoted Luan Richeng, general manager of Chinatex Raw materials Import and Export Corp, a subsidiary of the China National Textiles Import and Export Corp, as saying.
China imported 198,000 tonnes of wool in January-November 1996, a drop of 22.6 percent compared with the year-ago period.
Total wool imports for last year were expected to be 210,000 tonnes, down by 25.5 percent from the 282,000 tonnes imported in 1995, Luan said.
